Observed at +10.172647714614868s — page 9
://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/connect-an-mcp-server.md): Starts a connection request for an MCP server URL.
Discovery, browser consent, and validation happen asynchronously; poll the returned `connectionRequestId` until the status is term
inal. When the next step belongs to a person, the response carries a `handoffUrl` to open.\n- [Get a connection request](https://d
ocs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/get-a-connection-request.md): Current state of one connection request. Metered on
its own poll budget rather than the shared per-caller one, so polling on a short interval is expected and will not spend the budge
t your other calls need. A 429 here means the poll interval itself is too fast; honour Retry-After.\n- [Cancel a connection reques
t](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-connections/cancel-a-connection-request.md): Stops a request and invalidates its h
andoff link. Cancelling an already-terminal request is a no-op.\n- [Retry validation](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server
-connections/retry-validation.md): Re-arms a stalled validation immediately instead of waiting out its backoff. Does not revive a
terminal request — after `failed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`, start a new one.\n- [List personas](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-refe
rence/swarms/list-personas.md): The project's personas, newest first. Archived personas are excluded.\n- [Create a persona](https:
//docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-persona.md): Creates one persona. To draft several with a model first, use `POST /
projects/{projectId}/personas/generate` — that route persists nothing.\n- [Get a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/sw
arms/get-a-persona.md): A persona that lives in a DIFFERENT project answers 404, never 403 — the route is not an existence oracle
for a project you cannot see.\n- [Delete a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/delete-a-persona.md): Refused wit
h 409 while goals still reference this persona — deleting it would strand them.\n- [Update a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-
reference/swarms/update-a-persona.md): Partial update. Goals reference the persona by id, so renaming one does not disturb anythin
g pointing at it.\n- [Draft personas with a model](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/draft-personas-with-a-model.md): R
eturns DRAFTS and persists nothing. That separation is deliberate: generation is the step most likely to produce something nobody
wanted, and a route that both invented and saved would make \"let me see what you'd suggest\" indistinguishable from \"fill my pro
ject with these\".\n- [Draft journeys for a persona](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/draft-journeys-for-a-persona.md)
: Returns DRAFTS and persists nothing — see `POST /projects/{projectId}/personas/generate` for why, and for the quota this counts
against.\n- [Get a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-journey.md)\n- [Archive a journey](https://docs.mcp
jam.com/api-reference/swarms/archive-a-journey.md): ARCHIVES rather than deletes, and the response says so. Existing runs keep poi
nting at the definition they executed, so their history stays readable.\n- [Update a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-referenc
e/swarms/update-a-journey.md): Editing a goal never disturbs a run already under way: a run pins its own immutable snapshot of the
definition at launch.\n- [List swarms](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/list-swarms.md)\n- [Create a swarm](https://d
ocs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-swarm.md): A swarm is an authoring container holding DEFAULTS for the goals made unde
r it. Creating one starts nothing.\n- [Get a swarm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/get-a-swarm.md)\n- [Archive a swa
rm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/archive-a-swarm.md): ARCHIVES the container. The goals authored under it are not
touched — they keep their own definitions and stay launchable.\n- [Update a swarm](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/up
date-a-swarm.md): Changes the container's DEFAULTS. Goals already authored under it keep the values they were created with — this
is not a cascade.\n- [List journeys](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/list-journeys.md): The project's goals, newest f
irst. Archived goals are excluded.\n- [Create a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarms/create-a-journey.md): Create
s one goal: a persona pursuing a task against one or more environments. To draft several with a model first, use `POST /projects/{
projectId}/goals/generate` — that route persists nothing.\n- [List secrets](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/list-sec
rets.md): The project's credentials as METADATA ONLY — no value is returned by this or any other route. Shows the project-shared s
ecrets plus the caller's own personal ones; another member's personal secret does not appear at all, not even its name.\n- [Create
a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/create-a-secret.md): Store a credential so environments can grant it to r
uns. THE VALUE TRAVELS IN THE REQUEST BODY and becomes visible to whatever makes the call. The response is metadata only. Creating
a project-shared secret requires project admin; a personal one does not.\n- [Get a secret](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/
secrets/get-a-secret.md): One secret's metadata: delivery mode, host binding, sharing, and when it was last handed to a run. Never
its value. A secret from another project — and another member's personal secret — both read as 404.\n- [Delete a secret](https://
docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/delete-a-secret.md): Delete a stored credential. HARD — the row and the encrypted value both
go, and MCPJam stops delivering it. Deliberately NOT blocked when an environment still selects it: refusing would leave a leaked
credential undeletable until someone edited every environment naming it, and deletion must never wa…\n- [Rotate or re-bind a secre
t](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/secrets/rotate-or-re-bind-a-secret.md): Rotate the value and/or change how it is delivere
d. A rotation reaches NEW RUNS ONLY: a session already running holds the old value — materialized in its box's environment, or ins
ide an egress policy that cannot be read back — and there is no safe way to replace it mid-run.\n- [List a journey's runs](https:/
/docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/list-a-journeys-runs.md): Newest first. Compact records — `attempts` is on the single-ru
n read.\n- [Launch a journey](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/launch-a-journey.md): Answers **202**: the run row
exists and its fan-out has started. It is not finished — poll `GET /projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` until `status` leaves
`running`.\n- [Get a journey run](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/get-a-journey-run.md): The full record, includi
ng per-session `attempts` and `targetSummaries`.\n- [List a run's sessions](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/list-
a-runs-sessions.md): One entry per chat session the run produced. Summaries, not transcripts — read a transcript through the chat-
session routes using `id`.\n- [Cancel a journey run](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-runs/cancel-a-journey-run.md): Ac
cepts a durable Stop request and returns immediately. cleanupPending indicates that attempts are being settled in the background;
status remains the current stored run status. IDEMPOTENT: cancelling an already-cancelled run answers 200 with `alreadyCanceled: t
rue` and `finalized: 0`, not a 409.\n- [Project swarm roll-up](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/project-swarm-
roll-up.md): Recent runs with their goal-completion rates and repeat-failure findings, plus a project-wide trend. Deterministic an
d free — start here.\n- [Get a run's rubric scorecard](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/get-a-runs-rubric-scor
ecard.md): The deterministic rubric result for one run. No model, no spend.\n- [List swarm findings](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-r
eference/swarm-insights/list-swarm-findings.md): Criteria that keep failing, tracked across waves. One finding is one problem OVER
TIME — `occurrenceCount` and `status` carry the history, so do not treat repeat appearances as separate problems.\n- [Dismiss a f
inding](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/swarm-insights/dismiss-a-finding.md): Hides a finding from your view. ORTHOGONAL to
